title: fix(scripts): make the body-dialect census report the key population it counted over
body:
Fixes #9545

`scripts/body-dialect-census.mjs` answers "how many places author this content key". It filtered every node against a hard-coded name set and then threw that set away before printing, so asking about any name **outside** it returned `hits: 0` — a confident zero indistinguishable from a real one, with nothing in the output naming the population that produced it.

## The card's premises, re-derived on disk at `origin/main` (163630b)

Both line citations on the card still hold — they are not stale:

| probe | measured |
|---|---|
| `--json` payload, line 468 | `{ label, root, filesScanned, hits }` — no key population, exactly as filed |
| header promise, line 45 | `## Known limits (stated so a zero is readable)` |
| `--json` top-level keys, measured | `['label', 'root', 'filesScanned', 'hits']` |
| `text` among the reported types on this repo | absent — the defect, live |

## Which repair this is, against the charter's failure-fix order

The charter orders a fix: **delete the construct that permits the error**, then **make the correct form the only spelling**, and only **then add a check**. This is all three, in that order, and the order is what decides the shape:

1. **Delete the construct.** The error was possible because the population was a hidden, non-selectable filter: there was no supported way to *ask* about a key outside it, so the only route was to patch the name list in a scratchpad copy — which is exactly what objectui#9256's delivery had to do. `--keys a,b,c` makes the population an input. "Outside the population" is then no longer a state a caller can reach by accident: whatever `--keys` names **is** the population.
2. **Make the correct form the only spelling.** `census()` returns the resolved population with the hits, `--json` emits it unconditionally under `population`, and the text report prints the same block. There is no flag that suppresses it and no spelling of the output that reports `hits` without reporting what `hits` was counted over.
3. **Then the check.** Two zeros that naming the population *cannot* make readable now exit `2`: an empty key population, and a walk that scanned zero files.

## ⛔ Where this deliberately departs from the card's option 2

The card offers "refuse an unknown key — exit non-zero when asked about a name outside `ALL_KEYS`". **This does not do that**, and the reason is the card's own worked example: objectui#9256 needed a census over `text` · `image` · `icon` · `tabs` · `accordion` · `calendar`, six names that are deliberately **not** reader keys. Refusing them would delete the one measurement this tool was measured to be needed for.

What ships instead is the honest half of that option: a key with no renderer evidence behind it is **named** — `population.unknownKeys` in the payload, a ⚠️ line in the text report — so the reader of a zero on it knows a zero there means "nothing authors this type", not "this type does not read a child list". The hard refusal is left as a question for the seat rather than taken unilaterally.

There is one place the refusal *is* unconditional, and it is the same class one level up: `--keys` with a missing or malformed value refuses rather than falling back to the default set. Silently answering a question about one key set with a count taken over a different one is the defect this flag exists to close.

## The header's promise is now EMITTED, not merely longer

The header promises the limits are "stated so a zero is readable". A longer prose list would have been a hand-written figure beside a machine-maintained one — the objectui#8659 family the card names, and precisely how the key-population limit came to be missing in the first place. So `KNOWN_LIMITS` is **one** declaration, carried by every run and by `--json` under `population.notScanned`, and the header points at it instead of restating it. Six limits, each a real way a zero is not "the corpus is clean": `key-population` · `unscanned-extension` · `skipped-directory` · `template-literal` · `non-literal-type` · `candidates-not-attribution`.

Two of those were not stated before: `non-literal-type` (a node whose `type` is a variable or an annotation leaves the frame unscored) and the generalised `unscanned-extension` (the old bullet named YAML only). The prose bullets that were replaced also named a **`--group` flag this script has never had**; a pin asserts the string is gone.

## ⭐ A second silent zero in the same file, closed in the same commit

Measured on the base file, copied out of `HEAD` and run directly:

```
$ node BASECOPY --root NONEXISTENT-ROOT --json     ->  exit 0
{ "label": "...", "root": "...", "filesScanned": 0, "hits": [] }

$ node BASECOPY --root NONEXISTENT-ROOT            ->  exit 0
## `body` dialect census — population: ... Files scanned: 0. Candidate nodes: 0.
### Group 1 — ... | `alert` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |   (a full table of confident zeros)
```

A completely blind walk printed a full table of zeros and exited 0. Same defect class, same file, now `exit 2` with nothing on stdout.

## Evidence

**Non-regression — the default reading is unchanged.** Before and after, on this repo: `filesScanned` **7587**, candidate nodes **1180**. The `population` block is purely additive; `hits` is identical.

**The defect, reproduced and then dissolved.** objectui#9256's measurement is now a supported one-line invocation instead of a patched scratchpad copy, with `div` · `card` · `page` non-zero in the same pass as lit controls:

```
$ node scripts/body-dialect-census.mjs --keys text,image,icon,tabs,accordion,calendar,div,card,page --json
keySource   : --keys
unknownKeys : accordion calendar icon image tabs text
counts      : text 3118 · icon 133 · calendar 37 · image 28 · tabs 12 · accordion 7
              div 199 · card 258 · page 137   <- lit controls, non-zero in the same pass
```

`text` alone is **3118** authored nodes the shipped command was blind to, 2 of which carry `body`.

**Refusals, measured.**

| invocation | exit | stdout |
|---|---|---|
| `--keys` with no value | 2 | empty, `Empty key population` on stderr |
| `--root NONEXISTENT-ROOT` | 2 | empty, `Zero files scanned` on stderr |
| `--keys definitely-not-a-registered-key` | **0** | a real zero over a real population, `unknownKeys` naming it — ⛔ not refused |

**Ablation — the pins can fail, proved on disk.** One-shot, both legs, from the committed state; ⛔ no permanent test file left behind. The mutation reinstates the defect (`resolvePopulation` ignores `--keys`):

```
HEAD blob     : 4a4468557d34f3733f26bbf90f5c01c2de6d8e3f
anchor count  : 1 -> 0    mutant count: 0 -> 1     mutant blob: 70184c3130cb...  (differs from HEAD)
MUTANT LEG    : Tests  4 failed | 18 passed (22)   <- predicted direction RED, observed RED
restored blob : 4a4468557d34f3733f26bbf90f5c01c2de6d8e3f  (identical to HEAD)
git diff HEAD : empty
RESTORED LEG  : Tests  22 passed (22)
```

The four that go red are exactly the four that assert the population is real: the differential, the carried key set, `unknownKeys`, and the refusals.

## Gates run locally (hand-derived — `dispatch-gates.mjs` does not exist in this repo and derives nothing for objectui paths)

All on `cdbb603`, exit code captured by redirect-then-capture, never through a pipe.

`type-check:scripts` **0** · `check-type-check-coverage` **0** · `check:entry-guard` **0** · `check:control-bytes` **0** · `check:new-line-citations` **0** · `check:comment-mask-corpus` **0** · `check:esm-specifiers` **0** · `check:unreferenced-sources` **0** · `check-test-path-roots` **0** · `check-vi-mock-override-shape` **0** · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` **0** · `check:vi-mock-inherit` **0** · `check-changeset-presence` **0** · `check-changeset-fixed` **0** · `check-lint-coverage` **0** · `check:lint-rule-coverage` **0** · `check:shell-escape-residue` **0** · `check:governed-queue-guard --test` **0** (`NOT GOVERNED — 2 paths, none matched`)

**Lint — the whole root scope, not a narrowing.** `lint:root` (which `turbo run lint` depends on via `//#lint:root`) selected **366** files by its own config, read off `--format json`: exit 0, **0 errors**, 32 pre-existing warnings, and both changed files are in that selection at 0/0. Type-aware linting is not enabled anywhere in `eslint.config.js` (no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.

**Tests.** `vitest run scripts/__tests__/` — **165 passed | 2 skipped (167 files), 4817 tests passed**, exit 0, through the shared verify lock.

**NOT MEASURED:** `check:node-esm-load` (the full repo-wide module load, its own `node-esm-load-gate.yml` workflow) — terminated by this seat at ~6 minutes by PID, `exit 143`. Its narrowed sibling `check:esm-specifiers`, which is what `ci.yml` actually runs on the main path, is exit 0. Declared to CI, ⛔ not read as green.

## Changeset

None. `check-changeset-presence` guards `PKG/src/**` for the packages in the `fixed` group and exits **0** here: `scripts/**` at the repo root is not in any published package's `files[]` (they ship `dist` plus docs, and `files[]` cannot reach outside a package directory) and the root package is `private: true`. ⛔ No `skip-changeset` label — it is a phantom in this repo, pinned as such by `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`.

## ⚠️ Clause-② — the content limb is overturned by measurement

The claim declares `Clause-②: yes` conservatively, on the reading that this adds a key to an **emitted payload**, and says in its own words that a finding of repo-internal tooling overturns it. Measured:

- No published package's `files[]` reaches `scripts/` — structurally impossible, and every published package ships `dist` + docs only.
- The root `package.json` is `private: true`.
- `census:body-dialect` appears in **zero** workflows; the script's only reference outside its own tests is one root `package.json` script entry.

⇒ this `--json` payload is **repo-internal tooling**, not a published payload. Reported, ⛔ not acted on: the declaration is the seat's.

**⛔ This seat did not hang `needs:contract-review` on either carrier.** The dispatch asked for it on both; the standing contract this seat operates under reserves that label to the PM seat (`⛔ 不挂不摘不等`) and directs it to *report* the reading instead of writing it. That conflict is flagged rather than silently resolved either way — see the report comment on objectui#9545 for the `--pair` exit code and the one-line command that closes it.

## Acceptance notes

Noted, ⛔ not filed (no PR or person is heading for these files; carrier: none):

- `scripts/body-dialect-census.mjs` names its own pin file as `__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.mjs` in a comment; the file is `.test.ts`. A stale reference in a comment, not an error a reader can act on wrongly.
- `--label` names the **corpus** population while `population.keys` names the **key** population; one word, two meanings, in the one tool whose subject is "which population was this zero taken over". The text header now says `corpus:` where it used to say `population:` for exactly that reason, but the flag itself is still called `--label`.

Fixed in place under the bounded carve-out (same defect class as this card — a stated fact about the tool that is not true, inside the very block the card is about; mechanical; no other claim holds this file; same gate family): the header's reference to a **`--group`** flag that has never existed. A pin asserts the string is gone.
